is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles arabiensis, a member of the Anopheles gambiae complex (Page 1, Abstract).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study reports genotyping for Vgsc L995F (kdr L1014F), Vgsc L995S (kdr L1014S), Vgsc N1575Y (N1570Y), and Ace-1 G119S (G280S) (Page 4, Methods; Page 5, Results).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 2 provides genotype counts (SS, RS, RR) and allele frequencies for kdr L1014F in multiple populations (Page 7).

african_field_population.evidence: The study uses field-collected Anopheles arabiensis from nine sites in Ethiopia (Page 2, Methods; Page 3, Fig 1).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical research paper reporting original field and laboratory data (Page 1).

sub_country_location.evidence: The study provides data for nine specific study sites: Mankush, Chewaka, Tolay, Asendabo, Bako, Sodore, Shellemele, Goro, and Guba Hora (Page 2, Methods; Page 3, Fig 1).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The study reports collection years from 2013 to 2015 (Page 3, Methods).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study describes new collections and primary data analysis.

supplement.evidence: All necessary genotype data is provided in Table 2 of the main text.

assessment.summary: This study monitored insecticide resistance in Anopheles arabiensis across nine sites in Ethiopia from 2013 to 2015. It performed WHO bioassays and genotyped for kdr (L1014F, L1014S, N1575Y) and Ace-1 (G119S) mutations. It also assessed metabolic resistance mechanisms (GSTs, esterases, P450s). High kdr L1014F frequency was found, and elevated GST activity was detected in some populations.
